From 531353e650db087e61ce84f8e6b7e0982c1dc1b0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2021 15:57:26 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] iommu: Update "iommu.strict" documentation

Consolidating the flush queue logic also meant that the "iommu.strict"
option started taking effect on x86 as well. Make sure we document that.

Fixes: a250c23f15c2 ("iommu: remove DOMAIN_ATTR_DMA_USE_FLUSH_QUEUE")
Signed-off-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/2c8c06e1b449d6b060c5bf9ad3b403cd142f405d.1623682646.git.robin.murphy@arm.com
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>

diff --git a/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt b/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
index cb89dbdedc46..20a32de990ed 100644
--- a/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
+++ b/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
@@ -1987,7 +1987,7 @@
 			  forcing Dual Address Cycle for PCI cards supporting
 			  greater than 32-bit addressing.
 
-	iommu.strict=	[ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
+	iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
 			Format: { "0" | "1" }
 			0 - Lazy mode.
 			  Request that DMA unmap operations use deferred
@@ -1998,6 +1998,10 @@
 			1 - Strict mode (default).
 			  DMA unmap operations invalidate IOMMU hardware TLBs
 			  synchronously.
+			Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the
+			equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict
+			mode explicitly specified by either method takes
+			precedence.
 
 	iommu.passthrough=
 			[ARM64, X86] Configure DMA to bypass the IOMMU by default.
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt**
   - The documentation for the `iommu.strict` kernel parameter has been updated to reflect that it now applies to both ARM64 and x86 architectures. 
   - The line describing the parameter was changed from:
     ```
     iommu.strict=	[ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
     ```
     to:
     ```
     iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
     ```
   - Additional notes were added to clarify that on x86, the default behavior is influenced by driver-specific parameters, but that explicitly specifying strict mode takes precedence.

### Relationships

- The changes in the documentation are directly related to the consolidation of the flush queue logic, which allowed the `iommu.strict` option to take effect on x86 systems as well. This patch ensures that the documentation accurately reflects this new behavior, thereby improving clarity for users and developers regarding the functionality of the `iommu.strict` parameter across different architectures.

Here is the commit message:
iommu: Update "iommu.strict" documentation

Consolidating the flush queue logic also meant that the "iommu.strict"
option started taking effect on x86 as well. Make sure we document that.

Fixes: a250c23f15c2 ("iommu: remove DOMAIN_ATTR_DMA_USE_FLUSH_QUEUE")
Signed-off-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/2c8c06e1b449d6b060c5bf9ad3b403cd142f405d.1623682646.git.robin.murphy@arm.com
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of documentation indicating that the `iommu.strict` option was applicable to both ARM64 and x86 architectures after the consolidation of the flush queue logic. This oversight could lead to confusion among users regarding the behavior of the parameter on x86 systems, as it was previously only documented for ARM64.

 			Format: { "0" | "1" }
 			0 - Lazy mode.
 			  DMA unmap operations invalidate IOMMU hardware TLBs
 			  synchronously.
+			Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the
+			equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict
+			mode explicitly specified by either method takes
+			precedence.
 
 	iommu.passthrough=

The documentation only specified that the `iommu.strict` option was applicable to ARM64, which created confusion for users regarding its applicability on x86 systems after the flush queue logic was consolidated. This oversight could mislead users into thinking that the option was not relevant for x86 architectures.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```plaintext
+	iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
+			Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the
+			equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict

+			precedence.
```
Reason:
The patch updates the documentation to explicitly include x86 in the `iommu.strict` option description, clarifying that it is applicable to both ARM64 and x86 architectures. Additionally, it provides important context about the default behavior on x86, ensuring users understand how the strict mode interacts with driver-specific parameters. This resolves the confusion and ensures accurate usage of the option across different architectures.
